items.markdown:
When it comes to rare and collectible children's literature, value is driven by **first editions, low print runs, author inscriptions, and historical significance**.

#### 🏆 The Record-Holders: Most Expensive & Valuable

1. ***The Tales of Beedle the Bard* by J.K. Rowling ($3.97 Million / £1.95 Million)** 
	- **Why it’s valuable:** One of only **seven** hand-written and hand-illustrated copies created by Rowling, bound in Moroccan leather with mounted moonstones. Purchased by Amazon at a [Sotheby's](https://www.sothebys.com/) auction.[[1]](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/429442-most-expensive-childrens-book-sold-at-auction)
2. ***Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone* (1st Edition, 1st Printing, 1997) ($150,000 to $1.75+ Million for special association copies)** 
	- **Why it’s valuable:** Only 500 copies were printed in the very first hardback run (300 of which went to public libraries). Copies inscribed by J.K. Rowling or featuring unique publisher/illustrator ties command astronomical prices. Track market listings through rare dealers like [Raptis Rare Books](https://www.raptisrarebooks.com/product/harry-potter-and-the-philosopher-s-stone-jk-rowling-first-edition-signed-rare-association/).[[1]](https://www.raptisrarebooks.com/product/harry-potter-and-the-philosopher-s-stone-jk-rowling-first-edition-signed-rare-association/)
3. ***The Adventures of Tom Sawyer* by Mark Twain (1876, 1st American Edition) (~$25,000 – $35,000+)** 
	- **Why it’s valuable:** First issues in original cloth binding (and rare presentation copies) are cornerstones of American literature collecting, frequently cataloged by specialists like [Bauman Rare Books](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/).[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/)
4. ***The Runaway Bunny* by Margaret Wise Brown (1942, 1st Edition) (~$32,000)** 
	- **Why it’s valuable:** Early children's picture books from the golden mid-century era in pristine dust jackets are notoriously hard to find surviving in collectible condition.[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/)
5. ***East of the Sun and West of the Moon* illustrated by Kay Nielsen (1914, Signed Limited Edition) (~$29,000)** 
	- **Why it’s valuable:** Prized heavily for its elaborate, ethereal Golden Age of Illustration artwork rather than just the text.[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/)

#### 📚 Other Iconic Collectible Titles & Est. Ranges

- ***Make Way for Ducklings* by Robert McCloskey (1941, 1st Edition):** ≈ $19,500 (dependent on dust jacket condition).[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/)
- ***Wonderful Stories for Children* by Hans Christian Andersen (1846, 1st English Translation):** ≈ $17,000.[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/children/)
- ***Charlie and the Chocolate Factory* by Roald Dahl (1964, 1st US Edition):** Look for the **six-line colophon** on the final page to verify true first-printing status.
- ***The Velveteen Rabbit* by Margery Williams (1922):** Early printings with William Nicholson’s original lithograph illustrations can range from hundreds to several thousand dollars depending on the state of the cover.

#### 🔍 How to Tell If a Children's Book Is Valuable

- **Check the Copyright Page:** Look for a "First Edition" statement or a number line that counts down to 1.
- **Dust Jacket Condition:** In modern children's books (post-1930s), a missing or torn dust jacket can slash the value of a book by 80% or more.
- **Ex-Library Stamps:** While early Harry Potter library copies still have value due to extreme scarcity, stamps or card pockets generally lower the collector ceiling for standard vintage books.
